title: Angela Lansbury
wiki_lead:
Dame Angela Brigid Lansbury (16 October 1925 – 11 October 2022) was an Irish-British and American actress and singer. In a career spanning 80 years, she played various roles across film, stage, and television. Although based for much of her life in the United States, her work attracted international attention. 
Lansbury was born into an upper-middle-class family in central London, the daughter of Irish actress Moyna Macgill and British politician Edgar Lansbury. To escape the Blitz, she moved to the United States in 1940, studying acting in New York City. Proceeding to Hollywood in 1942, she signed with Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM) and obtained her first film roles in Gaslight (1944), National Velvet (1944), and The Picture of Dorian Gray (1945). She appeared in 11 further MGM films, mostly in minor roles, and after her contract ended in 1952, she began to supplement her cinematic work with theatrical appearances. Lansbury was largely seen as a B-list star during this period, but her role in The Manchurian Candidate (1962) received widespread acclaim and is frequently ranked as one of her best performances. Moving into musical theatre, Lansbury gained stardom for playing the leading role in the Broadway musical Mame (1966), winning her first Tony Award.
Amid difficulties in her personal life, Lansbury moved from California to Ireland's County Cork in 1970. She continued to make theatrical and cinematic appearances throughout that decade, including leading roles in the stage musicals Dear World, Gypsy, and Sweeney Todd, as well as in the Disney film Bedknobs and Broomsticks (1971). Moving into television in 1984, she achieved worldwide fame as the sleuth Jessica Fletcher in the American whodunit series Murder, She Wrote, which ran for 12 seasons until 1996, becoming one of the longest-running and most popular detective drama series in television history. In 1989, Corymore Productions, a company that she co-owned with her husband Peter Shaw, began co-producing the series with Universal, and Lansbury also became its executive producer during its final four seasons. She also moved into voice work, contributing to animated films like Beauty and the Beast (1991) and Anastasia (1997). In the 21st century, she toured in several theatrical productions and appeared in family films such as Nanny McPhee (2005) and Mary Poppins Returns (2018).
Among Lansbury's accolades are six Tony Awards (including a Lifetime Achievement Award), six Golden Globe Awards, two honorary BAFTA Awards, a Laurence Olivier Award, an honorary SAG Award, and the Academy Honorary Award, in addition to nominations for three Academy Awards, 18 Primetime Emmy Awards, and a Grammy Award. In 2014, she was made a dame by Queen Elizabeth II.

grok_lead: Angela Lansbury (October 16, 1925 â October 11, 2022) was a British-American-Irish actress and singer renowned for her versatile performances across theater, film, and television over an eight-decade career. Born in London to a prominent familyâher grandfather was Labour Party leader George Lansbury and her mother was actress Moyna Macgill âshe fled to the United States with her family during World War II, eventually settling in Los Angeles and becoming a U.S. citizen in 1951. Lansbury's breakthrough came in 1944 with her film debut in Gaslight, earning her first Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress at age 18, followed by two more nominations for The Picture of Dorian Gray (1945) and The Manchurian Candidate (1962). Her stage career solidified her as a Broadway icon, beginning with her 1957 debut in Hotel Paradiso and culminating in a record-tying five Tony Awards for leading roles in Mame (1966), Dear World (1969), Gypsy (1975), Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street (1979), and a 2009 revival of Blithe Spirit, plus a Lifetime Achievement Tony in 2022. She also received a Laurence Olivier Award for her 2015 West End performance in Blithe Spirit. In film, Lansbury appeared in over 60 movies, including memorable roles as Aunt March in Little Women (1949), the magical Miss Price in Bedknobs and Broomsticks (1971), and the voice of Mrs. Potts in Disney's Beauty and the Beast (1991), earning six Golden Globe Awards throughout her career. Her television legacy is dominated by the role of amateur sleuth Jessica Fletcher in Murder, She Wrote (1984â1996), which ran for 12 seasons, garnered 12 consecutive Emmy nominations, and became one of the highest-rated drama series of its time. Lansbury's personal life included two marriagesâfirst briefly to actor Richard Cromwell in 1945, then to producer Peter Shaw from 1949 until his death in 2003âand she raised three children, including stepson David. Honored with an Honorary Academy Award in 2013 for her lifetime achievement, she was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire in 1994 and Dame Commander in 2014, reflecting her enduring influence on the arts. She passed away at her home in Los Angeles at age 96, leaving a profound legacy as one of the most acclaimed performers of her generation.
